fields.label: EOD Sync Filter Help
fields.options:
How Selective EOD Sync Works:
  • If this table is empty, EOD Sync will process all eligible MOP Logs created today.
  • If rows are added, EOD Sync will process only the selected Manufacturing Work Orders / Operations from the configured Sync From Datetime onward.
  • Previous-day MOP Logs and logs before Sync From Datetime will not be processed.

fields.label: EOD Sync Work Order Filter
fields.options: MOP EOD Sync Work Order Filter

fields.label: Stock Reconciliation Window Help
fields.options:
How the Stock Reconciliation Window works:
  • Set From Time / To Time on each Department.
  • While a department's window is open: Stock Reconciliation for it is allowed, and all other stock movement touching it is blocked.
  • Outside the window: stock movement is allowed and Stock Reconciliation is blocked.
  • A department with no From/To Time set is never restricted.
  • Unchecking the box below disables the whole feature immediately.

fields.description: Master switch. When unchecked, no reconciliation-window restriction is applied anywhere.
fields.label: Enforce Stock Reconciliation Time Window
Casting Tree Re-Issue Help
fields.options:
How Full Casting Tree Re-Issue works:
  • Work orders cast on one tree share a Casting Group, stamped on the first Casting Issue.
  • When the box below is checked: a later Casting Issue touching that group is blocked at submit unless the Employee IR carries every work order cast together. Use Load Full Casting Tree on the Employee IR to pull in the missing members in one click.
  • When unchecked (the default): a partial re-issue is allowed. The subset moves onto a new Tree Number while the rest stay on the old one, so the old tree's Material Details ledger may never reach Received.
  • Load Full Casting Tree stays available either way — it is a convenience, not a guard.

fields.description: Master switch. When unchecked, a Casting Issue may carry only part of a casting tree. When checked, an Issue touching a casting group must carry every work order cast together.
fields.label: Enforce Full Casting Tree Re-Issue

fields.options:
Why the EOD transfer is split
A single very large Material Transfer cannot be saved and submitted in a reasonable time: ERPNext creates one Stock Ledger Entry document per row and revalues inline as it goes, and each Stock Reservation Entry re-aggregates its whole item/warehouse into Bin. One real run produced a 26,489-row draft worth ₹10.66 cr that never submitted before the lock expired.

The bucket is therefore split into chunks bounded by both caps below, whichever is reached first. Each chunk is its own Stock Entry and is committed on success, so earlier chunks survive a later failure — and a failed chunk is halved and retried down to a single Work Order, so one bad Work Order strands only itself.

A Manufacturing Work Order is never split across chunks. A single Work Order larger than the row cap forms its own oversized chunk.

Set both caps to 0 to restore the old one-Stock-Entry-per-bucket behaviour. Reference points: ERPNext itself moves Stock Reconciliation to the background above 100 rows, and the largest EOD Stock Entry this system has ever submitted successfully had 152 rows.

fields.description: Maximum Manufacturing Work Orders per EOD Stock Entry. 0 = no limit on this axis.
fields.label: Max Work Orders per Stock Entry

fields.description: Maximum item rows per EOD Stock Entry. 0 = no limit on this axis. A single Work Order is never split, so a Work Order with more rows than this still forms one chunk.
fields.label: Max Rows per Stock Entry

fields.description: Stop starting new work this many minutes into a run, then finish cleanly and release the lock. Must stay inside the 4-hour lock window so the graceful stop beats the hard job timeout. 0 disables the deadline (not recommended — a run that overruns is then killed hard and leaves the lock to the hourly reaper).
fields.label: Soft Deadline (minutes)

fields.options:
Why a separate catch-up pass exists
The scheduled run scans today only and fires once a day. A MOP Log created after tonight's run therefore sits in a window no later scheduled run will ever scan again — it only ever showed up in the read-only old unsynced MOP Log count. That is how a backlog of roughly 647,000 rows across ~12,939 Work Orders built up, and why clearing it needed a hand-built manual run over a huge date range.

The today-only window is unchanged. After the main pass finishes cleanly, this drains the oldest pre-window Work Orders, up to the cap below, through exactly the same plan → allocate → chunk → commit pipeline.

It is skipped when the main pass reported blocking failures or the soft deadline has passed — a run already in trouble does not take on more work.

Watch Old Unsynced MOP Log Count run over run: it is the honest progress signal. If it is not falling, raise the cap or give the drain its own off-hours window.

fields.description: After the main pass, drain the oldest pre-window unsynced MOP Logs (bounded by the cap below).
fields.label: Enable Backlog Catch-up

fields.description: Maximum Manufacturing Work Orders drained from the backlog per run, oldest first. 0 disables the catch-up pass.
fields.label: Max Backlog Work Orders per Run

fields.options:
How EOD Stock Allocation works
Stock is validated per Manufacturing Work Order, but each EOD Stock Entry consumes the sum across the MWOs it carries — so two MWOs that each fit can jointly overdraw a batch and fail the transfer.

When enabled, MWOs are admitted against a run-wide running tally of physical batch stock and warehouse headroom, oldest unsynced MOP Log first. An MWO that does not fit is deferred to the next run (reported as Deferred - Bucket Stock Contention). An MWO that cannot fit even on its own is reported as Permanently Short — a data defect needing reconciliation.

Keep this ON. With chunked Stock Entries an over-subscribed chunk strands only itself, so contention fails quietly instead of loudly; this tally is what prevents it. Turn OFF only to reproduce the old all-or-nothing behaviour.

fields.description: Admit MWOs into the EOD transfer against a run-wide running stock tally; defer the ones that do not fit instead of failing the chunk. Load-bearing once chunking is on — turn OFF only to reproduce the old all-or-nothing behaviour.
fields.label: Enable EOD Stock Allocation

fields.options:
How Plan-Phase Reservation Heal works
When an EOD row has no active Stock Reservation Entry, its whole Manufacturing Work Order is held out of the transfer — even though the batch is usually still physically in stock.

When enabled, the sync tries to re-create the missing reservation at the warehouse that physically holds the batch, then re-plans the MWO once. Each attempt is wrapped in its own savepoint and fails safe: if no warehouse has enough free batch qty, or the batch is Customer Goods belonging to a different customer than the Sales Order, nothing is created and the row stays a Missing SRE failure.

This submits real Stock Reservation Entries. Leave OFF until you have verified a run with it enabled on a staging site.

fields.description: Re-create missing WIP reservations during planning instead of holding the whole MWO. Submits real Stock Reservation Entries — enable deliberately.
fields.label: Enable EOD Plan-Phase Reservation Heal
